To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Sim to real transfer is possible with a single model, (2) Simulated environments can be used as a proxy for real environments, (3) Simulated environments are a valid training ground for the real world, (4) The use of a simulator is a valid way of training robots, (5) Simulators are not just toys, they can be used for real world applications.
the use of an incremental environment complexity strategy for training reinforcement learning agents in simulation is a very efficient method to reduce the reality gap.

(1) a Soft Actor Criticism (SAC) based training strategy using incremental complexity of the simulated environment can be successfully applied to the real world; (2) this strategy is more efficient than a naive strategy in the real world; and (3) it is more efficient than domain randomization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How can we transfer a learning based model trained in simulation to a physical robot?
the transfer of a model free learning policy from a simulation to the real world.
the transfer of a depth based navigation policy trained in simulation to the real world.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper presents an interesting approach to reduce the reality gap for reinforcement learning.
the proposed approach is able to reduce significantly the need of fine tuning in the real world by 50%.
the incremental complexity strategy is able to reduce significantly the need for real fine tuning, while maintaining an acceptable level of performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, by incrementally adding complexity to the training environments, the agent is able to generalize to the real world with little additional training.
a model-free policy trained in simulation can be transferred to the real world with little or no additional training.
the incremental environment complexity approach is a powerful tool to reduce the reality gap in reinforcement learning and can help to reduce the cost of training a robot in the real world.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed training strategy is able to produce a relevant navigation policy with only a few minutes of training in the simulator.
incremental complexity training can be a simple yet effective way to improve transfer performance.
the use of incremental complexity can be an effective strategy to reduce the reality gap and to improve the sample efficiency in a reinforcement learning context.
